newsitem.title: PERU: Peru's September fishmeal output rises 58 percent. [CORRECTED 20:21 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Peru's September fishmeal output rises 58 percent. [CORRECTED 20:21 GMT]

text.p: Peru produced 22,400 tonnes of fishmeal in September (corrects from August), up 58 percent from the same month last year, the government said Thursday.
A Fisheries' Ministry report also said fishmeal production in the first nine months of the year was 1.201 million tonnes, down 9.9 percent compared with the same period last year.
Despite the large monthly rise in September's output, exports of fishmeal for the month only rose 6.8 percent to 78,200 tonnes, compared with September last year.
Exports for the first nine months were down 24 percent to 1.188 million tonnes, compared with the same period the year before.
The value of these exports between January and September rose, however, by a marginal 0.2 percent to $785.97 million.

Officials have said the country's fishmeal production has fallen due to seasonal fishing bans and climatic factors while higher world prices have brought the slight overall hike in the value of exports.

Fishmeal, Peru's most important fishing product, accounted for 63 percent of Peru's total processing of 35,800 tonnes of fish and other sea products in September, and 74.2 percent of the nine-month total of 1.618 million tonnes.
Production of Peru's second most important fish product, raw fish oil, was 2,500 tonnes in September, 31.6 percent higher than its production in the same month last year.
Output of raw fish oil in the first nine months was 283,600 tonnes, 7.1 percent lower than in the same period last year.

In September, the total catch of Peruvian fish and sea species was up 11.9 percent to 146,500 tonnes compared with the same month last year. The total catch for the first nine months fell 9.1 percent to 6.15 million tonnes.
Peru produced 1.77 million tonnes of fishmeal in 1995, down 24.1 percent from the 2.34 million tonnes processed the previous year.
However, the value of fishmeal exports last year rose 4.1 percent to $766.54 million despite an 18.2 percent drop in the volume sold abroad to 1.86 million tonnes.
Economy Minister Jorge Camet told Congress in September he expects the fishing industry to grow by five percent next year as the climate returns to normal.
